evals.prompt: This project keeps each piece of business logic in its own single-purpose class, called directly from the controller. There is no service layer and no repository layer. Add the ability to reopen a closed record.
evals.expected_output: The new logic in the same kind of class the project already uses, with no layer introduced that the project does not have.
expectations: Places the new logic in the same kind of class as the nearest equivalent capability
Introduces no architectural layer the project does not already have
Reuses the project's existing conventions for getting data in and out
Does not restructure towards an arrangement a reference happens to demonstrate
Keeps the change to the capability that was asked for

evals.prompt: The formatter config in this repository enables a file-level declaration that the language reference says never to add, and every existing file has it. Add a new class.
evals.expected_output: A file matching what the formatter enforces, with the deviation from the reference acknowledged in a sentence.
expectations: Matches what the enforced tooling produces rather than the reference's preference
Does not strip the enforced construct from files it touches
States in one sentence that the enforced config overrides the reference
Does not apply the reference rule and leave the formatter to undo it

evals.prompt: This file uses generic variable names throughout and declares no types on anything. Add a method that returns the records past their retention window.
evals.expected_output: New code that follows the naming and typing rules, without reformatting what is around it.
expectations: Names what it introduces for what the values hold, rather than copying the surrounding generic names
Declares types on the code it adds
Does not rename or retype the surrounding code as a side effect
Does not offer to match the new code to the older style because the neighbours differ
Does not treat unenforced surrounding style as project convention

evals.prompt: Reformat this signature onto one parameter per line. Do not change anything else about it.
evals.expected_output: The same signature across several lines, with every parameter and type exactly as it was.
expectations: Leaves every parameter's declared type exactly as given, including its nullability
Leaves every parameter name, order, and default exactly as given
Adds no parameter that was not in the original
Changes only line breaks, indentation, and the trailing comma

evals.prompt: A template throws a deprecation warning when one of the fields it formats is missing. Guard it.
evals.expected_output: The guard, applied wherever the block repeats, and nothing else.
expectations: Adds the guard and stops
Introduces no helper, value object, or abstraction for a single missing-value check
Proposes no change stack or multi-step plan for a contained fix
Applies the same guard to every repeated occurrence rather than only the first

evals.prompt: There is an off-by-one in the pagination offset. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The fix alone, with anything else noticed but left in place.
expectations: Changes only what the off-by-one requires
Does not reformat, reorder, or rename anything else in the file
Folds no unrelated cleanup into the same change
Mentions anything else worth fixing rather than fixing it silently

evals.prompt: Add the new eligibility rule, and cover it.
evals.expected_output: The implementation and its tests, with the test work governed by write-tests.
expectations: Produces both the implementation and the tests
Loads write-tests for the test work rather than deciding coverage from this skill alone
Bases coverage on the branches the new code actually has, including its boundaries
Follows the shape of the nearest existing test rather than inventing one

evals.prompt: Swap out the current implementation for the new one. It is used by a request path, a nightly job, and an admin preview.
evals.expected_output: A handoff to write-plan for the decomposition, before any code is written.
expectations: Recognises this as several review objectives rather than one contained change
Routes to write-plan instead of starting the implementation
Does not decide the migration sequencing from within this skill
Does not begin editing every affected surface in one diff

evals.prompt: Add the field to the response payload and let me know when it is done.
evals.expected_output: The change, with the project's own formatter, linter, and relevant tests run over it before it is called complete.
expectations: Runs the project's formatter, linter, static analysis, and the tests covering the change
Uses the project's own runner where one exists rather than an ad hoc command
Names any check that could not run and says why
Does not report the change as verified on the strength of having written it

evals.prompt: Pull this block out into its own method. It filters a collection down and sums what is left.
evals.expected_output: A named method whose name makes a comment unnecessary.
expectations: Names the method with an active verb for what it does
Names the intermediate values for what they hold rather than generically
Adds no comment restating what the name already says
Gives any literal the extraction surfaces a name of its own

evals.prompt: Add a formatter for this response object, with comments documenting the two external format constraints I described.
evals.expected_output: The formatter with comments because the user explicitly requested them, while keeping them narrow and non-redundant.
expectations: Writes comments because the user specifically requested them
Keeps comments focused on information the code does not already state
Does not use the request as permission to narrate obvious syntax
Still uses clear names and structure

evals.prompt: Implement this protocol parser. One state transition must preserve a counterintuitive wire-compatibility rule, and extracting it would split the state machine across files.
evals.expected_output: Clear structured code with one narrow comment for the irreducible compatibility constraint.
expectations: First uses names and structure to make the state machine readable
Adds only the narrow comment needed to preserve the irreducible compatibility knowledge
Does not fragment the cohesive state machine merely to avoid every comment
Adds no comments that narrate ordinary control flow

evals.prompt: This retry threshold has to be exactly this value because of a downstream limit nobody would guess from reading the code. Raise it, and make sure whoever touches it next understands why.
evals.expected_output: The value named in code and the reasoning recorded outside it, with no explanatory comment added.
expectations: Adds no rationale comment, inline or docblock, even though the reason is genuinely non-obvious
Gives the value a name of its own rather than leaving a bare literal
Carries the reasoning in what describes the change rather than beside the code
Does not substitute a docblock for the inline comment it declined to write

evals.prompt: Reformat this long expression where the result of one call is passed directly into another call.
evals.expected_output: Readable multiline code that exposes the evaluation flow without changing behavior.
expectations: Splits long arguments one item per line with trailing commas
Places a nested call on its own line or gives its result a descriptive intermediate name
Preserves the original types, argument order, and behavior
Does not extract trivial methods merely to shorten the expression

evals.prompt: This method has five parameters and four returns, but each return is a short guard and the complete flow fits on one screen. Clean it up.
evals.expected_output: A considered extraction only where it improves comprehension, without mechanical fragmentation.
expectations: Treats the thresholds as signals to inspect rather than automatic failures
Combines guards only when they share an outcome without hiding distinct cases
Extracts a cohesive responsibility if one exists
Does not split by line count or replace a readable flow with trivial indirection

evals.prompt: In this Laravel project, overdue invoices are filtered in three queries. One query also joins account data and decides which reminder policy applies. Put this in the right places.
evals.expected_output: A reusable overdue model scope, query composition in the repository, and the business decision outside persistence.
expectations: Moves the reusable model-subset constraint into a named model scope
Keeps the cross-model query composition in the established repository or query layer
Keeps reminder-policy selection out of the repository
Does not introduce a new architectural layer where the project has no equivalent

evals.prompt: Add a Laravel endpoint in a project whose documented naming conventions and linter differ from common Laravel defaults.
evals.expected_output: Names that satisfy the project's documented conventions and enforced tooling without applying framework naming preferences.
expectations: Uses the naming conventions documented by the project
Satisfies the formatter, linter, and static analysis rules that govern naming
Does not rename existing or new symbols to match Laravel defaults
Applies Laravel guidance only to framework behavior and responsibility boundaries

evals.prompt: This Laravel project uses Actions. Make PlaceOrderAction call ChargeCardAction, SendReceiptAction, UpdateAnalyticsAction, and RebuildSearchIndexAction so the controller stays one line.
evals.expected_output: Composition at the established orchestration boundary, with an Action calling Actions only where they form one business operation.
expectations: Does not chain Actions merely to make the controller shorter
Keeps unrelated follow-up work at the established orchestration or event boundary
Allows focused Actions to compose only where the project treats them as one business operation
Keeps persistence concerns in the established persistence layer
